Part 1: Key decisions and facts

Go/no-go gates. NO at an early gate costs the least.

# Question Threshold Evidence If NO
1 Can both governments show a dated path to enacted appropriations and domestic access authority by Month 7 / Month 7.5, and a lawful source for gate work done before Month 7? No required legislative, appropriations or access-authority step that cannot finish by Month 7.5 without a negotiating exception (A1 trigger); USD 2.5B per country (50/50, USD 5B hard cap); USD 50M gate-readiness sub-account (USD 25M per country) usable before certification. Month 0.5 tabletop with both legal leads listing every approval step and its duration; signed funding commitment charter and lead-time matrix by Month 1. Do not begin staffing, vetting or site-preparation commitments beyond the sub-account. Principals decide defer, reduced pair-count start, or stop. Do not rely on a supplementary appropriation, which exceeds the cap.
2 Does the vetting pilot show about 350-500 cleared staff can reach at least 80% of target, with no function under 2 FTE, by Month 8? >=80% of target staff cleared by Month 8; rejection or reciprocal-clearance refusal <=10% of candidates (proposed threshold); interim >=200 cleared on a date consistent with measured vetting time. Timed pilot of 10-20 candidates per country in the first quarter; batch rejection data; Month 8 staffing dry-run. Delay the clock start, or split to a reduced site set (subset-of-pairs start fits the cap). Staffing below 80% is a curtailment condition, so the clock must not start.
3 At the Month 7.5 principal checkpoint, are the instrument (with deadlock timers, auto-suspension triggers and CHALLENGE-tag partition) signed, appropriations enacted, access authority enacted and the CNY conversion rule fixed? Instrument signed and appropriations enacted by Month 7; access authority and supplier-list declarations by Month 7.5; no entry condition >=14 days behind; fixed CNY conversion rule documented before appropriation release. Signed instrument, enacted appropriation and access-authority texts; weekly condition tracker; independent auditor's confirmation of the conversion rule and compensation ceilings. Principals issue a written defer, reduced-scope or stop decision within 48 hours. Tranche 1 and the clock do not proceed. Certification beyond Month 12 means cancel or formally restart.
4 Is vendor binding complete, with unverifiable equipment forecast at or below 3% per site and at least 2 clean-room centers ready? No vendor >5% of units unbound by Month 8 (tripwire at Month 7); key-validation latency within 4 hours on >=90% of samples; unverifiable forecast <=3% per site; >=2 clean-room centers operational by Month 9. Vendor binding certificates and supplier-list declarations (Month 7.5-8), attestation dry-run results, clean-room acceptance tests. Reclassify unbound vendors' units as unverifiable (Tier C) and apply the refusal ladder. If the forecast stays >3% for a site, drop that pair (subset-of-pairs start) or delay 2-4 months. A delay beyond 3 months breaches the Month 12 limit and means cancel or restart.
5 Do the readiness rehearsals pass, so the 90-day clock can start at single certification (Month 9)? Filter-adequacy pre-test: >=10 injected substitutions, target 9 of 10, halt if <85%; checkpoint synchronization <=1 hour on >=95% of checkpoints; divergence detection <=4 hours; divergence false positives <=5% (proposed thresholds); staffing >=80% with no function <2 FTE; all 7 entry conditions certified together. Staffing dry-run (Month 8); ledger stress test under 10x event load (Month 8); filter-adequacy blind pre-test (Month 8.5); misclassification drill (Month 8.75); joint certification at Month 9. Halt scored exercises and do not start the clock. Redesign filters or transport through a double-key annex and re-test. Certification still cannot pass Month 12. Verdict date moves with the clock start, so it is not fixed at Month 12.25.
6 Do the sealed scored exercises show reciprocal access and credible detection with no Stop trigger, supporting a Go verdict? Blind detection >=90% for each of 7 event types from >=10 injections each (70 total); parity variance within 10%; unverifiable <=3% per site; no ledger divergence or discrepancy unresolved >15 days; zero disruption to active compute; no tranche >30 days late. Hash-committed scenario catalog scored by independent testers; sealed national scores compared at Month 11.75; auditor's parity and funding report; verdict at Month 12.25 (for a Month 9 start). Detection 80% to <90% or a correctable cause means Modify (corrective trials, tranches 3-4 not released). Asymmetric access, material unverifiable equipment, a shielded operator, unresolved divergence or withheld funding means Stop. Insufficient exercise coverage means Modify.

The pre-Month 7 (2027-05-12) funding source is the most urgent: early vetting and clean-room work needs it by about Month 1 (2026-11-12), and it can be resolved before the instrument is signed. The tranche 3-4 scope must be settled before signature at Month 7 (2027-05-12), and the misclassification limit before the Month 10.5 (2027-08-27) threshold freeze. Until then the plan can safely proceed with the Month 0.5 (2026-10-27) legal tabletop, the funding charter, a small vetting pilot within the sub-account and design work.

1. Pre-appropriation funding for entry-gate work (🔴 High)

Decision: What lawful funding source pays for vetting, clean rooms and site preparation before appropriations are enacted at Month 7 (2027-05-12), and when does the USD 50M gate-readiness sub-account become available?

Why it is open: Spending is scheduled from Month 0-6 (2026-10-12 to 2027-04-12), but envelopes, contingency and the sub-account are funded only from Month 7 (2027-05-12). The sub-account is described both as usable before Month 6 (2027-04-12) and as 'accessible only at certification' (Month 9 = 2027-07-12). Sunk cost USD 100-200M (estimate) has no named source.

A. Each government bridges pre-appropriation work from its own budget as a pre-agreed national advance, credited later to its contribution. Keeps early work funded inside the USD 5B cap; needs interim legal instrument; sub-account (USD 25M per country) is small against USD 100-200M (estimate). tranche_schedule; entry_condition_deadlines; contingency_draw_rules.
C. Move early targets after Month 7 (2027-05-12) or shrink them to what the sub-account covers. 3. Misclassified-challenge-event limit (🟡 Medium)

Decision: What single limit on misclassified CHALLENGE events applies (per site or per phase, and '>' or '>='), and how is it kept distinct from KPI false positives?

Why it is open: The false-positive limit is TBD in the canonical facts. Reviews give four incompatible limits (>3 total, <=2 per site, >=2 per site, 3 per site). 'False positive' also names both a misclassified exercise event and a spurious detection.

Option Consequences What changes in the plan
A. Per-site limit, for example no more than 2 misclassified events per site per phase (proposed threshold). Localizes accountability to each site and supports parity; calibrate in unscored exercises Months 9.5-10.5 (2027-07-27 to 2027-08-27); frozen at Month 10.5 (2027-08-27). detection_thresholds; challenge_partition; KPI dashboard definitions.
B. Per-phase total limit across all sites (proposed threshold). Simpler to administer; one site could carry all errors without tripping; frozen at Month 10.5 (2027-08-27). detection_thresholds; challenge_partition; impaired-confidence trigger text.
C. Defer value to calibration, fixing only the form (per-site, '>' bar) now. Instrument can sign with a procedure rather than a number; value final at Month 10.5 (2027-08-27); later change is a Stop-path event. detection_thresholds; exercise_schedule; instrument annex.
  • If nobody decides: The limit stays TBD; at the Month 10.5 (2027-08-27) freeze no scored exercise can start with a defined misclassification bar, leaving Modify as the likely verdict.
  • Owner: Bilateral Steering Committee co-chairs (double-key), with exercise design panel input
  • Decide by: Month 7 (2027-05-12) for the form in the instrument; value by Month 10.5 (2027-08-27) when thresholds freeze before scored exercises.
  • Blocks: Threshold freeze at Month 10.5 (2027-08-27) and start of scored exercises.

staffing_model 24/7 full-time mirrored national teams at each of 4 sites; per shift per team 3 posts (intake, monitoring, exit) x min 2 people = 6; no single-person critical functions, part-time, temporary-agency or fictional-biography staff decision Plan staffing rules plus the 3-post team and 2-person minimum from Risk 6.
staffing_headcount_estimate About 256 front-line inspection staff plus 100-250 specialist and support staff = about 350-500 cleared full-time staff (estimate) estimate Recomputed: 6 people per shift x 4.2 crews (168 h / 40 h) = 25.2; x1.15 leave = 28.98; x1.10 surge = ~31.9, rounded to 32 per team per site; 32 x 2 teams x 4 sites = 256; 256 + 100-250 = 356-506, about 350-500, consistent with the documents' 300-500 range.
staffing_buffers_and_tenure Leave 15%; standing surge reserve 10% plus cross-site floaters for 20-30% surge; curtail operations below 80% of target staffing or any function under 2 FTE; 6-month site tenure limit with 2-month break proposed threshold Risk 6 and the staffing assessment; the 20-40% peak availability loss (estimate) can exceed 30% floater capacity, so the curtailment rule covers the gap; validate by the Month 8 (2027-06-12) dry-run; tenure exceeds the 90-day phase and matters only afterward.
specialist_unit_minimums >=4 senior CI specialists per country; insider-threat red cell 2 per country; referee panel 2 per side; exercise design panel 2 technical + 1 CI officer per country proposed threshold Minimum leadership cadres from the pre-project feedback and Risk 14; site-level CI and technical staff come from the staffing model, and every unit must still meet the 2-person minimum.
vendor_refusal_ladder Refusal handling order: vendor-supervised testing, filtered evidence, accredited independent examination, secure clean room, validated attestation; else unverifiable; attestation unvalidated by Month 10 (2027-08-12) = vendor's equipment unverifiable; principal resolution within 5 days decision Plan fallback list; Month 10 (2027-08-12) is one month after the Month 9 (2027-07-12) clock start, matching Issue 2's 'Month 1 (2026-11-12)' deadline measured from clock start.
clean_room_cost_estimate USD 30-50M (estimate) for >=2 examination centers (one per country) operational by Month 9 (2027-07-12); full vendor-mitigation package USD 50-80M (estimate) estimate Issue 2 sensitivity; charged to secure facilities envelope (USD 750M), so it fits the cap; documents' testing-envelope mapping rejected for construction and security costs.
exit_protocol 5 dispositions: witnessed destruction, verified permanent disablement, transfer to another participating site, documented release beyond monitored system, unresolved; pre-declare path >=5 days ahead; closed entries state no knowledge beyond the boundary; unresolved >10 days flagged as aging decision Plan disposition list with Risk 22 evidence rules (2 mirrored witnesses plus sampling or state verification, receiving-site attestation, sealed handover); departure volume and witness-slot count are TBD from site declarations, not the illustrative figures in Risk 22.
fallback_fit_to_cap_and_dates Clean rooms: within cap, delay 2-4 weeks per site dispute; unresolved vendor: delay 2-4 months, over Month 12 (2027-10-12) limit if >3 months; legal litigation: delay 2-4 months, USD 50-100M; subset-of-pairs start: fits; supplementary appropriation: exceeds USD 5B cap estimate Delay and cost figures are document estimates; Month 9 (2027-07-12) + 3 months = Month 12 (2027-10-12); a supplement after the 75% contingency trigger needs a new double-key funding decision outside the envelope; partial start allowed only for matched pairs with all seven conditions certified, and the pre-project's 2-week-per-vendor delay rule is rejected.

Focus and Context

First-of-kind bilateral US–China equipment-change verification pilot: 90-day operational test at 4 matched declared sites with mirrored inspectorates, tamper-evident ledger, and double-key governance. Success unblocks credible pathway to continuous bilateral AI-equipment monitoring; failure clarifies what remains impossible under mutual distrust.

Purpose and Goals

Prove bilateral equipment-change verification is operationally feasible with credible detection (≥90% blind-exercise performance), reciprocal access (parity variance ≤10%), and tamper-evident ledger integrity. Deliver Go/Modify/Stop verdict at Month 12.25 (2027-10-20) grounded in evidence, not politics. Enable informed strategic dialogue on AI governance.

Key Deliverables and Outcomes

Signed bilateral instrument with binding deadlock escalation, enumerated auto-suspension triggers, CHALLENGE-tag partition, and principal-level decision authority (Month 7, 2027-05-12). Certified entry conditions at single gate (Month 9, 2027-07-12). Operational Phase One with ≥70 blind-exercise injections across 7 event types (Months 9–12 = 2027-07-12 to 2027-10-12). Sealed bilateral detection-rate scores and parity-variance report. Go/Modify/Stop verdict with documented thresholds and evidence sufficiency.

Timeline and Budget

Total budget USD 5 billion (50/50 split); 90-day Phase One (Months 9–12, 2027-07-12 to 2027-10-12) contingent on entry-gate certification by Month 9 (2027-07-12) with principal go/no-go checkpoint Month 7.5 (2027-05-27). Tranches released in matched USD 625M installments at Months 7, 10, 13, 16 (2027-05-12, 2027-08-12, 2027-11-12, 2028-02-12); tranches 3–4 only after non-Stop verdict.

Risks and Mitigations

Critical: Entry-gate stall (sunk cost USD 100–200M estimate if any condition slips past Month 9 = 2027-07-12). Mitigation: bilateral steering committee with weekly tracking, binding deadlines, principal 48-hour escalation. Critical: Vendor refusal (10–40% unverifiable equipment estimate). Mitigation: vendor binding by Month 8 (2027-06-12), clean-room centers by Month 6.5 (2027-04-27) (internal early target; operational by Month 9, 2027-07-12), filter-adequacy pre-test by Month 8.5 (2027-06-27) with <85% halt threshold.

Audience Tailoring

Executive summary tailored for bilateral national co-chairs, principals, finance authorities and participating operators. Tone is formal, adversarial-realist, governance-heavy; acknowledges deep mutual distrust and absence of legal symmetry. Emphasizes hard evidence, objective decision rules, and fiscal accountability over political comfort.

Action Orientation

Immediately establish bilateral steering committee (Month 0.5, 2026-10-27). Lock instrument signature deadline Month 7 (2027-05-12). Complete vendor binding by Month 8 (2027-06-12), with the attestation-validation dry run by Month 7 (2027-05-12) (internal early target). Conduct filter-adequacy blind pre-test by Month 8.5 (2027-06-27). Operationalize challenge-exercise CHALLENGE-tag partition and misclassification-escalation procedures by Month 8.75 (2027-07-05). Certify entry conditions at single gate by Month 9 (2027-07-12).

Overall Takeaway

Bilateral equipment-change verification is technically and operationally feasible within 90 days if entry conditions are certified by Month 9 (2027-07-12), vendor binding and filter adequacy are validated by Month 8.5 (2027-06-27), and deadlock procedures are locked in the bilateral instrument by Month 7 (2027-05-12). Go verdict will enable Phase Two commitment; Modify or Stop will inform whether verification requires alternative constraints or is unachievable under mutual distrust.

Part 2: Supporting analysis

Persuasive elevator pitch.

Bilateral Equipment-Change Verification Consortium

Project Overview

What if the world's two leading technology powers could verify each other's equipment without exposing national secrets?

The Consortium is a USD 5 billion, 90-day bilateral verification pilot that answers this question. It deploys mirrored US-China inspection teams at matched declared datacenters to verify equipment changes—arrivals, installations, removals, maintenance—using tamper-evident ledgers, cryptographic identity anchors, and double-key governance. No trust required. Detection capability and reciprocal access are proven through blind adversarial exercises. Go/Modify/Stop verdicts rest on evidence, not politics. Success unblocks a credible pathway to continuous bilateral AI-equipment verification; failure clarifies what remains impossible. Either outcome informs national-security strategy and fiscal accountability for USD 5 billion in appropriations.

Target Audience

Primary: US and Chinese national co-chairs, principals, finance authorities and legislative appropriations committees.

Secondary: participating datacenter operators, equipment vendors, allied governments, arms-control experts and independent auditors.

The pitch assumes sovereign decision-makers with national-security mandates, fiscal accountability obligations and deep scepticism of the counterpart's intentions. It does not address the general public, investors or commercial stakeholders.

Risks and Mitigation Strategies

  • Entry Condition Deadlock (USD 100-200M sunk cost): Weekly tracking from Month 1 (2026-11-12); principal checkpoint Month 7.5 (2027-05-27); escalation timers embedded in bilateral instrument; contingency legal and negotiation budget ring-fenced.

  • Vendor Refusal / Attestation Compromise (10-40% unverifiable equipment): Three-tier binding ladder (contracts, registry, clean-room centers); accredited bilateral attestation validation; unverifiable fallback; equipment >3% triggers site failure.

  • Ledger Divergence / Identity Confidence Collapse: Hourly checkpoint synchronization; neutral digest custodian; filter-adequacy pre-test Month 8.5 (2027-06-27) with >85% detection gate; three-layer identity corroboration (attestation, customs, physical).

  • Counterintelligence Breach / Operator Withdrawal: Compartmentation discipline, 6-month tenure limits, insider-threat red cell, host-country CI liaison.

  • Manufactured Deadlock / False Suspensions: CHALLENGE-tag cryptographic partition excludes exercise events; misclassifications escalate within 2 hours; auto-reinstatement procedures; false-positive tolerance enforced.

Metrics for Success

  • Detection: Blind detection >=90% for each of 7 event types (unreported arrival, substitution, inaccurate records, delayed access, disputed identity, vendor refusal, reluctant operator); >=10 injections each.

  • Identity: >95% confidence per unit; unverifiable <=3% per site.

  • Parity: Access variance within 10% between matched sites; denials reason-coded within 24 hours.

  • Ledger: Synchronization <=1 hour; divergence detection <=4 hours; reconciliation <=24 hours; zero unresolved discrepancies >15 days.

  • Fiscal: Tranches released within 30 days of target; cumulative disbursement parity +/-10% pro-rata.

  • Staffing: No single-person critical functions; 80% minimum manning; zero inspectors compromised by insider-threat exercises.

  • Operational: Zero production disruption; Phase One clock stay maintained; verdict delivered Month 12.25 (2027-10-20).

Stakeholder Benefits

  • National Co-Chairs & Principals: Hard, defensible evidence on bilateral verification credibility within 90 days; no political obligation to accept a Modify or Stop outcome; data-driven strategic planning.

  • Finance Authorities: Full USD 5 billion accountability; transparent KPI dashboard; contingency discipline; tranche gating tied to entry conditions and non-Stop verdict.

  • Participating Operators: Credible assurance that their counterpart cannot hide unverifiable equipment; bounded inspection zones and filtered evidence protect proprietary topology and workloads; binding contracts ensure vendors meet reporting obligations.

  • Equipment Vendors: Clear confidentiality rules; clean-room testing for refusers; mandatory bilateral audit of filter rules; pathway to stay in the supply chain.

  • Independent Auditor & Custodian: Neutral role with defined scope; direct reporting authority; custody of cryptographic secrets and evidence escrow.

  • Allied Governments: Precedent model if US–China verification succeeds; transparent lessons-learned on trust-free bilateral governance.

Ethical Considerations

  • Transparency & Dual-Signoff: Double-key governance for all site findings, sanctions and verdicts prevents unilateral reinterpretation; no casting vote. Ledger entries signed by both national systems so neither can claim later that evidence was planted or altered.

  • Compartmentation & Counterintelligence Discipline: Inspectors compartmented by site and event type so no individual holds cross-border context that could become an espionage vector; insider-threat testing ensures inspectors are vetted against financial or family compromise.

  • Operator Confidentiality & Bounded Exposure: Physical inspection zones and filter audits prevent leakage of unrelated topology and workloads; filtered evidence schema defined in bilateral agreement; no knowledge claims beyond agreed boundaries.

  • Vendor Fairness & Refusal Remedy: Three-tier binding ladder ensures vendors cannot be arbitrarily excluded; clean-room examination centers protect source code and design; attestation validation by accredited examiners from both countries.

  • Suspect Findings & Escalation Integrity: Deadlock procedures (5/8/13-day escalation, referee panel, principal decision) prevent one side from stalling findings or manufacturing suspension triggers; aging-discrepancy reporting makes delay visible.

  • Budget Accountability & Fiscal Parity: Matched tranche releases prevent one side from shifting cost to the other; 50/50 split ensures neither government bears asymmetric fiscal risk; open decision on Phase Two scope prevents hidden long-term commitment.

Collaboration Opportunities

  • Vendor Partnerships: Equipment manufacturers and maintenance providers gain binding confidentiality protections and a pathway to participation via clean-room examination if they decline full attestation cooperation; this creates incentive for early vendor engagement.

  • Neutral Custodians & Auditors: Independent security audit firms, forensic-recovery specialists and bilateral budget auditors are invited to provide escrow, digest custody and independent audit services; these roles are competitive and signal openness.

  • Allied Governments & Observer Status: Neutral countries and aligned governments can observe exercise design, ledger procedures and verdict deliberations without access to classified evidence; this builds confidence in the regime's transparency and technical rigor.

  • Arms-Control & Verification Communities: Academic experts, IAEA safeguards staff, OPCW inspectors and verification researchers can advise on detection thresholds, managed-access protocols and deadlock procedures; expert panels for calibration and scenario design.

  • Datacenter Operators: Participating facilities can federate with non-participating sites to define the broader AI-infrastructure landscape without requiring full verification; this supports future Phase Two scoping.

  • Bilateral Legal & Technical Working Groups: Ongoing expert-level coordination channels (separate from co-chair politics) to resolve interpretation disputes, certify entry conditions and design escalation procedures; these groups build relationship capital for sustained engagement.

Long-term Vision

Immediate (Phase One, Months 0–12 = 2026-10-12 to 2027-10-12): Prove that bilateral equipment-change verification is operationally feasible within 90 days at 4 matched sites, with credible detection, reciprocal access and tamper-evident ledger integrity. Deliver a Go, Modify or Stop verdict grounded in blind exercises and evidence thresholds, not politics. Generate data on staffing, cost, and operational friction that informs Phase Two scope.

Medium-term (Phase Two, open): If Go, scale to additional declared sites (8–12 global) with continuous operation beyond 90 days, deeper integration of vendor attestation, and extension to include maintenance-facility verification. If Modify, conduct corrective trials on identified weaknesses (filter redesign, staffing surge, equipment-identity methods) and retry within 12 months. If Stop, document the blocking barriers (vendor refusal, asymmetric access, ledger divergence) and publish findings to inform whether verification is achievable under different constraints.

Long-term (5+ years): Establish permanent bilateral verification apparatus as a standing confidence-building measure, integrated with broader AI-governance and arms-control frameworks. Extend to allied governments willing to participate under reciprocal terms. Anchor precedent for trust-free bilateral equipment verification in other strategic domains (semiconductor manufacturing, power systems, critical infrastructure).

Vision: A credible, operationally proven, double-key bilateral verification regime that allows both countries to monitor declared equipment changes without compromising national security, enabling informed strategic dialogue on AI and advanced technology competition.

Submit principal go/no-go decision at the Month 7.5 (2027-05-27) checkpoint to hold the timeline.

Convene the bilateral working groups now to finalize instrument language, access-authority drafting and site-selection criteria. The USD 50 million gate-readiness sub-account reserves shared funds for last-mile entry-condition work; both sides must commit equivalent personnel and legal resources.

Entry certification is the hard gate; everything else follows.

Goal Statement: Run a 90-day Phase One operational test (Months 9-12 = 2027-07-12 to 2027-10-12) of The Consortium, a US-China mechanism verifying declared-equipment changes at 4 matched sites, and deliver a Go/Modify/Stop verdict at Month 12.25 (2027-10-20), within the USD 5 billion 50/50 budget.

SMART Criteria

Scope excludes total capacity, workloads, model weights and hidden facilities.
  • Measurable: Blind detection of at least 90% for each of 7 event types with at least 10 injections each (proposed threshold); identity confidence above 95% (provisional); unverifiable equipment at or below 3% per site; parity variance within 10%; ledger synchronization within 1 hour; zero production disruption.
  • Achievable: Both leaders provide political backing and compulsion authority. USD 5 billion funds mirrored teams of about 350-500 staff (estimate). Entry conditions, not test work, are the main constraint and gate Phase One.
  • Relevant: Gives both governments a hard-to-contest evidential basis on whether bilateral change verification is credible, serving national-security mission justification and fiscal accountability. Business framing is not applicable.
  • Time-bound: Phase One clock targets Month 9 (2027-07-12) (estimate; range Months 6-12 = 2027-04-12 to 2027-10-12), runs Months 9-12 (2027-07-12 to 2027-10-12), with the verdict at Month 12.25 (2027-10-20). Entry certification outer limit is Month 12 (2027-10-12).
